newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen not to use force in hostage standoff.
newsitem.headline: Yemen not to use force in hostage standoff.

text.p: Yemen said it would not use force while negotiations continued to free five Polish tourists held hostage by tribesmen in the country's mountainous hinterland, Poland's ambassador to Yemen said on Monday.

The tourists -- three men and two women between the ages of 50 and 64 -- were kidnapped on their way to archaeological sites in eastern Yemen last week. It was the second abduction of European holidaymakers this month.
"I have official confirmation from the Yemeni authorities that no force will be applied with the kidnappers while negotiations are going on," Ambassador Krzyfztof Suprowicz told Reuters.

The tourists were abducted by members of the Al al-Masni tribe in the Khawlan area, about 65 km (40 miles) east of the capital Sanaa. Diplomats said the abduction took place sometime between Tuesday and Thursday.
On Friday, the tribesmen fired rocket-propelled grenades at military forces who had surrounded them, killing three soldiers and wounding five.
Diplomats said villagers had also been wounded, but said they had received confirmation the hostages were unharmed.

Suprowicz said he had requested that the authorities to set up a direct telephone connection with the abducted tourists if it was technically possible so the embassy could check on their physical and mental well-being.
"The Yemeni authorities affirmed to me that they are being treated well," he said.
Yemeni authorities on December 19 freed five Dutch tourists who were abducted and briefly held by tribesmen while touring an area 240 km (150 miles) north of Sanaa.

In recent years, tribes in Yemen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped tourists or other foreigners to use as bargaining chips. The tribes' demands have usually involved land or water issues, and have rarely been political.
The current standoff is the first kidnapping involving the Al al-Masni tribe, which lives in the Beni Jabr area near Khawlan.
